question: Under whose reign was the maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music written?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aurangzeb:-**

 
 
• His​** reign** saw the **maximum number of books** in **Persian **on classical Indian Music written.
 
 
 
• Classical Indian Music:-
 
 
• It​ has a rich history and is deeply rooted in the Indian subcontinent's culture.
 
 
 
• Persian:-
 
 
• It ​was a significant language during the Mughal period and was widely used in administration and literature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jahangir:-

 
 
• He​ was also a patron of the arts and was known for his love for music, but his reign did not see as many Persian books on classical Indian Music written as Aurangzeb's.
 
 
 
• Akbar:-
 
 
• He​ was a great patron of art and music and was known for his liberal policies towards all religions.
 
• However, there is no evidence to suggest that his reign saw the maximum number of books in Persian on classical Indian Music written.
 
 
 
• Shah Jahan:-
 
 
• He was a patron of art and architecture and is known for building the Taj Mahal.
 
• However, his reign did not see as many Persian books on classical Indian Music written as Aurangzeb's.
